To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electrochemical properties of germanium halometallates are dependent on the cation, oxidation state and nature of the halometallate.
the reduction of germanium halometallate complexes is affected by the nature of both the cation and the halide co- ligand.
the cation, oxidation state and halide have a marked effect on the structural and electrochemical properties of germanium halometallates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and characterisation, in both the solid state and solution, of germanium halometallate complexes.
the synthesis, characterisation and electrochemistry of a range of germanium halometallate complexes.
probing the effect of the cation, the oxidation state of germanium and the halide co- ligand on the structural and electrochemical properties of germanium halometallate complexes.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the GeII halometalliates are less prone to cation–anionic association than the GeIV chlorometalliates, and that the reduction potential for GeIV–Ge0 couples is more cathodic for the chlorometalliates than for the halometalliates, whereas for the GeII species, the reverse trend is observed, i.e. the GeII– Ge0 reduction potential becomes more cathodic as the halide co- ligand is changed Cl→I.

the GeII–(halometallate) complexes are less prone to association than their GeIV–(halomethallate) counterparts and that the GeIV–(chlorometallate) species are more readily reduced than the corresponding GeII–(chlorometalate) complexes.
the GeII–Cl bond strength in [EMIM][EMIM][GeCl3] is significantly greater than the GeII–Br bond in [EMIM] [EMIM][GeVBr3], which in turn is stronger than GeII–I in [EMIM](EMIM)[GeVI].
The main takeaway from our work is that
the halometallates of germanium are highly versatile and that their properties can be fine-tuned by altering the cation, the oxidation state and/or the halide co-anion.
the cation, the oxidation state and the halide co-anion all influence the structural and electrochemical properties of the germanium halometallates.

, in general, halometallate complexes of germanium(II) are more difficult to reduce than the analogous germanium(IV) species, and the reduction potential is influenced by both the nature of the halometallate ligand and the cation.
